title: Free time 3
note: B2 vocab leaf, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane. Three predecessors own 87 words — a1_freetime (35), a2_freetime (31), a2_sports (21) — covering the activities themselves (football, swimming, guitar, concert, film, theatre, festival, gallery, competition) and the doing verbs. The sweep dropped get away, day trip, sightseeing, itinerary, festival, gallery, into, work out and camping; the corrected pool also caught **membership**, taught this morning by b2_suffixes_1 whose node is still `coming` — seventh self-collision avoided that way. What is left is the layer around the activity rather than the activity itself: how you talk about rest (leisure, spare time, unwind, wind down, recharge, downtime, socialise) and about being into something (keen on, enthusiast, amateur, have a go), the specific hobbies a B1 course skips (photography, pottery, knitting, gardening, DIY, jigsaw, hiking, climbing, collector), and the practical words for getting to an event at all (gig, exhibition, rehearsal, audition, box office, season ticket, sold out, book in advance) — that last group is what actually blocks a B2 speaker buying a ticket. C57 card 0 recaps Free time 1 and 2. C49 all 36 across three boards of 12. E10 Use is rewrite production; every underline reconstructs its answer.

cards.title: You already know
cards.note: Free time 1 and 2 gave you the activities — sport, football, swimming, guitar, band, concert, film, theatre, festival, gallery, competition, prize — and the verbs: play, watch, listen, read, travel, relax. Those carry the sentences here. What is new is everything around the activity: how you talk about resting, how you say you are into something, and how you actually get a ticket.
cards.note_cz: Free time 1 a 2 ti daly činnosti — sport, football, swimming, guitar, band, concert, film, theatre, festival, gallery, competition, prize — a slovesa: play, watch, listen, read, travel, relax. Ta slova nesou zdejší věty. Nové je všechno okolo: jak se mluví o odpočinku, jak řekneš, že tě něco baví, a jak si vlastně koupíš lístek.

cards.title: Three ways to say you like it
cards.title_cz: Tři způsoby, jak říct, že tě to baví
points: English has several ways to say you enjoy something, and they are not interchangeable.
**keen on** takes a noun or *-ing*; **enthusiast** is the person; **have a go** is trying it once.

rows: He plays as an **amateur** — not for money.
You should **have a go** at painting.
